title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. College weekend review: Tuesday through Saturday (Oct. 20-24), graded. Then next college weekend.

paragraphs: Every pick below is graded against the line printed on its card when the game kicked off, not the closing line. A push counts as neither a hit nor a miss.

What got graded: all 56 college games from Tuesday, Oct. 20 through Saturday, Oct. 24. Each recap starts with the card, then the plays that swung the cover and the total, then who called it and who missed it. Play detail comes from ESPN's official play-by-play, and every numbered source is listed in the sources file.

Two handicappers sit out by design. Follow The Money only makes a pick when the number moves at least a point from the open, so it had no side in 26 games and no total in 22. In The Trenches only makes a pick when it sees a trench signal, so it had no side in 32 games and no total in 32. Those games are not graded for them.

Card line: Florida International −10.5, total 45.5. The Cover Writer's card had Florida International −10.5 and the Under, projecting Florida International 28, Middle Tennessee 16. Final: Middle Tennessee 26, Florida International 23. Middle Tennessee won by 3, and the teams scored 49 points.

Middle Tennessee led for most of the night, and the Florida International side never got close to laying 10.5. Terrence Brown broke a 54-yard touchdown run with 2:06 left in the third quarter for a 23-16 Middle Tennessee lead, and Dominic Bourgeois added his fourth field goal, a 28-yarder, for 26-16. Florida International also had a 46-yard try blocked on the last play of the first half.

The total sat at 42 until JJ Kohl found Sterling Joseph for a 21-yard touchdown with 6:06 left. That made it 26-23 and 49 points, over the 45.5. Florida International at −10.5 asked a lot, and Middle Tennessee didn't go along with it.
Called it: The Formula and In The Trenches on Middle Tennessee +10.5, covered by 13.5 points. Letdown Watch on the Over 45.5, cleared it by 3.5 points.

Missed: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on Florida International −10.5, missed by 13.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Under 45.5, went over by 3.5 points.

Card line: Delaware −3, total 52.5. The Cover Writer's card had Delaware −3 and the Over, projecting Delaware 29, Missouri State 24. Final: Missouri State 38, Delaware 61. Delaware won by 23, and the teams scored 99 points.

This was a one-score game for a half and change. With Delaware up 38-35 midway through the third, Brandon Gorham recovered a fumble on a Jawarren Corbin sack of Henry Belin IV, and Nick Minicucci ran in from a yard out at 4:01 for a 45-35 lead. George Mullins and Jawarren Corbin then picked off Belin on back-to-back Missouri State series around a Jo Silver touchdown run that made it 52-35.
The over was never in doubt. The teams had 52 at halftime, and Silver's 12-yard touchdown catch at 12:53 of the third made it 59.

Sam Houston turned it over on downs at 9:54 of the fourth. MJ Dowdy's 1-yard touchdown at 4:00 got the Bearkats within 30-24, but that was as close as they got.

Liberty led 14-3 at halftime, and the third quarter settled it. Kennesaw State turned the ball over twice in that quarter on interceptions, Jaylon Coleman ran 9 yards for a touchdown and a 24-3 lead at 1:37, and the Owls turned it over on downs on the next series. Terron Kellman's 2-yard touchdown run in the fourth made it 34-3.

The under 49.5 cashed comfortably. Daniel Kinney's 28-yard field goal with 1:11 left was the last score, and the game ended with 40 points. Kennesaw State +11.5 needed points, and two third-quarter interceptions made it hard to get them.

In overtime Josh Hoover ran 4 yards for a touchdown and the extra point made it 13-6. Michigan's Tommy Carr threw incomplete on fourth down to end it. Indiana won by exactly 7, so Indiana −7 is a push.

The under got help from three missed field goals: Butkowski from 53 and 32, and Indiana's Paddy McAteer from 56. The game finished at 19 points against a 41.5 total. A push in overtime. All that defense and the ticket came back exactly where it started.

Horton's touchdown was the last score, and the game finished at 51 points, under the 51.5 by half a point. Without those offsetting flags, the over would have had a much better chance. Half a point under, thanks to a pair of holding flags. The over crowd will be checking the replay for a while.

paragraphs: Same rules as Part 1: card line at kickoff, and a push counts as neither a hit nor a miss. Here is how the week came out for everybody, in the usual card order.

The Cover Writer went 25-30-1 against the spread and 25-31 on totals. The push was Indiana at Michigan, 13-6 in overtime, which landed exactly on the number. The Cover Writer would like the record to show that overtime was not on the card.
The Formula went 26-29-1 on sides and 26-30 on totals. The arithmetic was fine. The football just declined to cooperate.
Next Man Up went 26-29-1 on sides and 27-29 on totals. It did a little better on the totals than on the sides, and it plans to keep doing the reading this week.
Letdown Watch went 28-27-1 on sides and 28-28 on totals. That is a winning week on sides, and Letdown Watch has already been reminded that a good Saturday is how a letdown starts.
Follow The Money went 14-16 on sides and 20-14 on totals, picking only when the number moved. When the money talked on totals, it mostly told the truth.
In The Trenches went 12-12 on sides and 8-16 on totals. The sides broke even. The totals are being sent back to the line of scrimmage for more film work.

Now the smack talk for Halloween Saturday. The early number has Ohio State −7 at USC with a total of 52.5, and that one should start a few friendly arguments. The Georgia-Florida game has Georgia −10.5 and a 56.5 total, and the only thing scarier than that spread is whoever has to pick against it. Notre Dame and Navy meet at Gillette Stadium with Notre Dame −30.5 on the board. Whoever loses that argument this week owes the group chat a sincere apology and a bag of candy.
